newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa suffers brief discomfort.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa suffers brief discomfort.

text.p: Mother Teresa, recovering in hospital from heart surgery and pneumonia, experienced brief discomfort overnight but then went back to sleep, doctors treating the revered nun said on Monday.

"She was uncomfortable at 0100 hrs (1930 GMT) for two or three minutes," the team of doctors treating 86-year-old Mother Teresa at Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said in a regular medical bulletin.
"After that she was all right. Otherwise, Mother (Teresa) had a good sleep," it said without elaborating.

Doctors said on Sunday that the Roman Catholic missionary, who underwent life-saving heart surgery on November 29, had suffered a slight setback on Sunday, and her bronchial pneumonia was not responding to treatment.
The previous week, long-standing lung and kidney problems had combined with an irregular heart-beat to complicate Mother Teresa's recovery from her third heart surgery in five years.
Clinic official S.K. Tiwari said Mother Teresa's brief discomfort had not worried doctors too much.
"It can happen from time to time," he said. "They're waiting for her general condition to stabilise."
Over the weekend, doctors decided to postpone a procedure aimed at stabilising Mother Teresa's heartbeat. They wanted to wait until she gained strength.
The doctors have warned that Mother Teresa's recovery may take a long time, and that she may never be as active as before.

Thousands of people all over the world revere Mother Teresa as a saint for her work with the ill, the poor and the dying. The Missionaries of Charity religious order that she founded runs 456 charitable homes in 111 countries.
